note: Section 15: async copy/prefetch feasibility, derived from the real source-level architecture study (architecture.json's async_transfer_findings_for_section_15) plus this phase's own copy_microbench.json measurements, which used plain (non-pinned) host memory throughout.
evidence: ggml_backend_tensor_copy_async(backend_src, backend_dst, src, dst) is public (ggml-backend.h:116) and the Vulkan backend genuinely implements ggml_backend_vk_cpy_tensor_async (ggml-vulkan.cpp:15872), not a stub -- confirmed by reading the real implementation body.
event_fence_support: ggml_backend_event_new/record/wait exist in the public API (ggml-backend.h) and Vulkan's async copy path uses a real dedicated transfer queue (ctx->device->async_use_transfer_queue) distinct from the compute queue when available -- genuine hardware-level overlap capability, not just an API surface.
graph_scheduler_integration: ggml_backend_sched already uses cpy_tensor_async internally for its own cross-backend input staging during multi-backend graph execution (ggml-backend.cpp:1664) -- the mechanism is production-tested inside ggml itself, not experimental.
cpu_thread_overlap_possible: not directly tested this phase; the async entry points return a bool (success/fallback) synchronously from the calling thread, so genuine overlap would require the caller to issue the async copy and do other CPU work before a later ggml_backend_synchronize -- architecturally possible, not exercised here.
vulkan_transfer_queue_behavior_exposed: partially -- device->async_use_transfer_queue is an internal Vulkan-backend field (not part of the public ggml-backend.h surface), so a MEMBRANE caller cannot directly query or force it; the caller only sees the effect (whether cpy_tensor_async returns true and actually took the fast path) indirectly.

critical_precondition_not_met_by_this_ph.finding: the Vulkan async host<->device path REQUIRES the host buffer to be Vulkan-pinned memory obtained via the backend's own host-buffer-type mechanism (ggml_vk_host_get) -- a plain malloc'd or std::vector-backed host buffer (which is what every probe in this phase used, including copy_microbench.cpp) causes ggml_backend_vk_cpy_tensor_async to return false, silently falling back to the SAME synchronous path ggml_backend_tensor_copy already uses.
critical_precondition_not_met_by_this_ph.implication: copy_microbench.json's measured bandwidth (0.6-1.4 GB/s, well below PCIe theoretical) is a SYNCHRONOUS-path number, not a fair test of the async path's real potential -- this phase did not measure genuine async/pinned-memory transfer performance, and that is a disclosed limitation, not a null result for async prefetch specifically.

answer_to_section15: async copy infrastructure genuinely exists in the pinned llama.cpp/ggml/Vulkan stack (real transfer queue, real event/fence primitives, already used internally by ggml_backend_sched) -- but getting its benefit requires pinned host memory, which none of this phase's probes allocated. A naive tiering implementation using ordinary host buffers would silently run entirely on the synchronous path measured in copy_microbench.json and decode_impact.json, and Section 14's worst-case scenario D numbers (up to 47% stall at ctx=16384) are the realistic cost profile for THAT naive path. Genuine async/prefetch overlap is plausible but unproven -- it is next-step work (pinned-buffer allocation via the host buffer-type API), not something this phase demonstrated.
